_comment: Every third-party dependency MEGATRON links, with the licence it was
approved under. ci/policy_check.py (LICENCE) fails the build on any
dependency in a build file that is not listed here.
WHY AN ALLOWLIST AND NOT A LICENCE-SCANNING SERVICE:
the policy gate is stdlib-only and offline by design, so that it runs
identically on a laptop and a runner and can never itself become a
supply-chain concern in a project whose entire pitch is not being
MagnusBilling. A network call to resolve a licence is a network call that
can be wrong, slow, or absent -- and a gate that silently degrades when
The cost is that adding a dependency requires a human to write a line
here. That is the intended cost. MEGATRON is proprietary and
distributed to licensees, so a GPL/AGPL/LGPL dependency is not a licence
problem to be discovered later -- it is a product that cannot ship.
Adding an entry means asserting you checked the licence of THAT VERSION.

org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib.why: The language runtime. Unavoidable, and Apache-2.0 throughout.

org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-test.why: Test only. Never linked into a shipped binary.

org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launch.why: Test only, never distributed. EPL-2.0 is a weak copyleft that reaches only the EPL'd files themselves, and this is a test-runtime dependency that is not linked into any shipped artifact.
